source_native_model.source_full_candidate_formula: TM_z ~ richness + D + FDQ + FRic + FEve + (1|season) + (1|site)
source_native_model.source_code_locator: archived code.R Figure 3 community-level trait-matching block

fixed_effect_sensitivity.reading: The positive FDQ association persists after absorbing every time-invariant site difference and common seasonal shifts.

within_site_model_free_sensitivity.reading: After subtracting each site's own mean FDQ and TM, seasons with above-site-average FDQ tend to have above-site-average corrected trait matching.

mechanistic_gain: FDQ varies continuously across multiple sites and seasons. The positive source-model and site-fixed-effect relationships provide a contemporary functional-exposure bridge between pollinator community structure and flower-pollinator trait matching that cannot be reduced to static island identity alone.
relation_to_binary_boundary: This continuous exposure does not identify a historical Oshima-Toshima causal boundary, but it supplies a mechanism-compatible axis that varies within geographic sites and therefore is less confounded with island identity than the binary regime label.
claim_boundary: Observational contemporary association only. Site fixed effects remove time-invariant site confounding but not time-varying weather/resources, measurement error, feedback within networks or historical selection. The result does not identify the historical cause of Campanula floral or breeding-system change.
